summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares preinstall=`node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is an obfuscator.io-style script that detects OS/arch/libc, downloads a per-platform Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it (unzip / PowerShell Expand-Archive / hand-rolled ZIP parser), chmods the binary 0o755, and invokes `bun math_init.js` from the package root. math_init.js is a 727KB obfuscated Bun-CJS blob (header `// @bun @bun-cjs` followed by a hex constant pool and shift-based string decoders such as WV8StW) that is not referenced by the README or the SDK's dist/, and whose behavior is opaque to Node-based inspection prior to execution. Installing an alternate language runtime specifically to execute an undocumented obfuscated sibling script bypasses standard Node-based supply-chain review of what runs at install time. The package identity also mismatches its stated purpose: package name `@hubsync/web-sdk-react` versus a README describing the `Verdocs Web SDK for React`, consistent with a hijack/typosquat framing rather than a legitimate SDK release. A React SDK does not require a Bun-compiled binary blob executed during `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
